_comment: The taxonomy of Christian traditions this app covers, as data.
THREE LEVELS: branch -> family -> denomination. Only the first two are
defined here. `branches` is the split-by-split backbone; `families` is the
granularity sources are filed under and the level the app displays.
Denominations are future work and will hang off `families` by parent.
WHY A FILE AND NOT A MIGRATION: the tradition list is a doctrinal
judgement, not a schema detail. Keeping it as data means the judgement can
be read, argued with and diffed without reading Python, and it means the
excluded groups are recorded next to the rule that excludes them instead
of living only in whoever remembered to leave them out.
Applied by tools/build_traditions.py. Dry run by default.

criterion.name: Nicene in substance
_comment: The test is doctrinal content, not creedal form. A group that teaches
the substance passes whether or not it recites a creed, which is why
the Brethren, the Restorationists and the Adventists are all in: their
non-creedalism is a conviction about creeds, not a denial of the
affirms: The Trinity — one God in three co-equal, co-eternal persons
The full deity and full humanity of Christ — true God and true man
The incarnation, atoning death, and bodily resurrection of Christ
proxy_tests: Baptism in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, in a form the historic churches recognise. Catholic and Orthodox recognition of a body's baptism is a strong signal: Baptist and Methodist baptisms are recognised, LDS and Jehovah's Witness baptisms are not.

The World Council of Churches basis — churches that 'confess the Lord Jesus Christ as God and Saviour according to the scriptures... to the glory of the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit' — is a usable pre-filter, because its basis is explicitly Trinitarian.

excluded.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
excluded.why: Non-Trinitarian Godhead theology — three separate beings, not one God in three persons.

excluded.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
excluded.why: Arian — denies the full deity of Christ.

excluded.name: Oneness Pentecostals
excluded.why: Modalist — denies the Trinity by collapsing the persons into modes. Distinct from the Trinitarian Pentecostal bodies, which are included.

excluded.name: Christadelphians
excluded.why: Non-Trinitarian; denies the pre-existence and deity of Christ.

excluded.name: Christian Science
excluded.why: Denies the Trinity, the incarnation and the bodily resurrection.

branches.name: The Undivided Church
branches.description: Scripture, the Fathers and the ecumenical councils — what every branch below inherits rather than what divides them. Not a branch in the historical sense; the place the material that predates the splits belongs.

branches.name: Church of the East
branches.description: Separated after the Council of Ephesus.

branches.name: Oriental Orthodox
branches.description: Separated after the Council of Chalcedon.

branches.name: Eastern Orthodox
branches.description: The autocephalous churches of the Byzantine tradition, in communion with one another.

branches.name: Roman Catholic
branches.description: The Latin Church together with the twenty-three Eastern Catholic Churches in communion with Rome.

branches.name: Protestant
branches.description: The families issuing from the Reformation, and the movements that came out of them.

branches.name: Other and Independent
branches.description: Bodies that sit outside the branches above and are admitted one at a time on the doctrinal test rather than by category.

families.name: Scripture
families.description: The biblical text itself, which every tradition in this library is interpreting.

families.name: Early Church
families.description: The Fathers of the first eight centuries, before and across the divisions below.

families.name: Ecumenical
families.description: The acts of the seven ecumenical councils and the local synods, received in common.

families.name: Universal
families.description: Creeds held across the traditions rather than by any one of them.

families.name: Oriental Orthodox
families.description: The Coptic, Syriac, Armenian, Ethiopian, Eritrean and Malankara churches, distinguished at the denomination level.

families.name: Eastern Orthodox
families.description: The autocephalous churches — Constantinople, Moscow, Antioch, Serbia, Greece, Romania and the rest — distinguished at the denomination level.

families.name: Catholic
families.description: The Latin Church.

families.name: Eastern Catholic
families.description: The twenty-three sui iuris churches in communion with Rome, keeping Eastern liturgy and canon law.

families.name: Reformed
families.description: One family at this granularity, as the polity differences that separate Presbyterian from Congregational do not separate their confessions — the Savoy Declaration is a Congregational revision of Westminster.

families.name: Anabaptist
families.description: Mennonite, Amish and Hutterite.

families.name: Brethren
families.description: Church of the Brethren and Plymouth Brethren. Non-creedal, and Nicene in substance.

families.name: Holiness
families.description: Nazarene, Wesleyan, Free Methodist and the Salvation Army. The Salvation Army practises no sacraments and is fully orthodox on the doctrinal test, so it is in: the criterion is what a body confesses about God, not how many sacraments it keeps.

families.name: Pentecostal
families.description: Trinitarian bodies only — Assemblies of God, Church of God (Cleveland), Church of God in Christ, Foursquare. Oneness Pentecostalism is modalist and is excluded.

families.name: Restorationist
families.description: The Stone-Campbell movement: Churches of Christ, Disciples of Christ, Christian Churches. Non-creedal on principle, and Nicene in substance.

families.name: Adventist
families.description: Seventh-day Adventists and the wider Advent movement. Non-creedal, and Nicene in substance: the Fundamental Beliefs affirm the Trinity, the full deity and humanity of Christ, and the bodily resurrection. The distinctives that mark the family off — the seventh-day Sabbath, the investigative judgement, conditional immortality — are not touched by the criterion, which asks what a body confesses about God and not what else it holds besides.

families.name: Moravian
families.description: Three distinct churches grouped at this granularity. Two of them predate the Reformation — the Waldensians by some three centuries — and joined it rather than issuing from it; they are filed here because that is where they ended up, not where they began. Separate them at the denomination level.

families.name: Quaker
families.description: The Religious Society of Friends.

families.name: Nondenominational
families.description: A category rather than a denomination, and kept as one deliberately: these congregations have no shared confessional document to hold, so what files here is the movement's own writing, not a body's official teaching.

families.name: Old Catholic
families.description: The Union of Utrecht churches, separated from Rome after Vatican I.

families.name: Messianic Jewish
families.description: Admitted body by body rather than as a movement. Most Messianic congregations are Trinitarian and pass the test; some are not, and the category is not uniform enough to admit wholesale.

families.name: Independent Catholic
families.description: Admitted body by body. Some independent Catholic jurisdictions hold the Nicene faith intact and some have drifted into esoteric or syncretist teaching; the apostolic-succession claim these bodies make is not itself the test, and does not substitute for it.
